newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Scab worries lift bids.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Scab worries lift bids.

text.p: Concerns that recent rains in the Dakotas and Minnesota will foster development of scab and other fungal diseases pushed durum wheat prices sharply higher on Thursday, cash dealers said.

"There's some concern about scab," a Minnesota dealer said. "It's been really wet and humid. We really don't know yet about the extent of the damage, but with these weather conditions it's almost a given we'll have problems."
Durum bids were up 10 to 45 cents a bushel in Minnesota and North Dakota. Bids for dark northern spring wheat fell slightly as MGE September wheat dropped two cents.

"This spring, part of the state (North Dakota) was very dry and with those drought conditions, a lot of the durum did not come in very even," said Wayne Carlson, director of livestock for the North Dakota Department of Agriculture. "The latest crop report showed a big decrease in expected yields in durum country.
"Now we've been getting excessive rains in the durum region," he added. "There's been some scab and other diseases."
